provides: Team workspaces and tenancy: personal and work workspaces with a role/capability mandate model (builtin owner/admin/member/viewer plus product roles declared in settings, namespaced capability strings with wildcard grants), email invitations with single-use tokens (public preview / decline / claim flow: an unregistered invitee gets a verified account via auth's login-grant seam), last-owner protection, per-workspace settings and storage quotas, member lifecycle events for business services (kick, role change), a billing entitlement seam that degrades to allow without billing installed, plus internal service-to-service membership and capability checks — the foundational scope other modules attach their workspace_id to.

gates.behavior: personal: ensure_personal_workspace(user) runs, the account becomes OWNER of a new Personal workspace; none: no workspace is created, the account has zero memberships until invited.

curated.summary: Controls what a freshly registered account gets when it showed up on its own (no invitation) — read by resolve_landing_workspace(user, origin="street"). "personal" (default) gives it its own Personal workspace and makes it that workspace's owner — the open self-serve / demo-cloud shape, unchanged from every release before this axis existed. "none" gives it no workspace at all: the account is a guest (permissions.is_guest) until an existing organization invites it — the closed-organization shape. Does not affect invited registrations, which always land through the separate accept-invitation path.
curated.business_label: What an un-invited signup lands with

extension_points.name: Workspace.settings
extension_points.summary: A JSON bag on every workspace, PATCHable through the workspace API — the sanctioned place for app-level per-workspace preferences without schema changes.

extension_points.name: AUTH_USER_MODEL
extension_points.summary: Standard Django user swap — owner/member/inviter FKs target settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL; the module resolves users via get_user_model(), never a concrete class.

extension_points.name: serializer_seams
extension_points.summary: Every public view declares request/response serializer seams (SerializerSeamsMixin) — subclass the view, override the attribute, remount the URL.

extension_points.name: role_capabilities
extension_points.summary: Declare product roles and their capability strings in STAPEL_WORKSPACES["ROLES"] (last-wins over the builtin four; owner is system-protected). Check them via has_capability/require_capability (in-service) or the workspaces.check_capability / check_membership comm Functions (cross-service, no import); frontends read GET /roles and my_capabilities.

extension_points.name: capability_levels
extension_points.summary: Raise individual capabilities to the high step-up level via STAPEL_WORKSPACES["CAPABILITY_LEVELS"] (merged over the builtin members.provision / workspace.security.manage); enforcement arrives with the provisioning wave.

surface.name: capabilities_for
surface.intent: Granted capability strings of a role — primitive behind role_has_capability.

surface.name: capability_level
surface.intent: "standard"/"high" step-up level of a capability — check before gating on step-up.

surface.name: capability_matches
surface.intent: Match one granted capability string (wildcards "*" and "prefix.*") against a requested one — reach for this instead of writing your own prefix/wildcard comparison; stapel-core's cross-service consumer helper mirrors this exact semantics.

surface.name: effective_capability_levels
surface.intent: Builtin capability step-up levels merged with the CAPABILITY_LEVELS override.

surface.name: effective_roles
surface.intent: Builtin roles merged with STAPEL_WORKSPACES["ROLES"] — read instead of merging the setting yourself.

surface.name: role_exceeds_rank
surface.intent: The invite/role-grant rank-guard (mandate-model vardict 2026-08-03): true if a role outranks the acting role, so a product-defined role below admin that still carries members.invite/members.role.change/members.provision cannot hand out a rank above its own. Call this before creating any membership, invitation or provision row that assigns a role; unknown ranks fail closed.

surface.name: role_has_capability
surface.intent: Does this role grant this capability, no membership needed — for role definitions/invite pickers.

surface.name: role_rank
surface.intent: Numeric rank of a role, or None — prefer role_at_least/role_exceeds_rank for yes/no.

surface.name: get_membership
surface.intent: Fetch a user's WorkspaceMember row (active by default; include_suspended=True also returns a suspended one, e.g. to render error.403.membership_suspended instead of a bare not-a-member 403) — defines what "active membership" means.

surface.name: has_active_mandate
surface.intent: True if the user holds an active (accepted, non-suspended) membership ANYWHERE, workspace-agnostic — the primitive behind is_guest; use it when the question is "has this account joined anything at all", not "is it a member of workspace W".

surface.name: has_capability
surface.intent: True if the user's active membership grants a capability — the everyday authorization check.

surface.name: is_guest
surface.intent: THE canonical guest predicate (mandate-model vardict 2026-08-03): true for an authenticated user with no active mandate anywhere — an anonymous session qualifies by construction. Branch dashboards/onboarding on this, never on request.user.is_authenticated.

surface.name: require_capability
surface.intent: Membership if the user holds a capability, else None — capability-gate for a view.

surface.name: require_role
surface.intent: Membership if the user holds at least a minimum role, else None — this module's own role-gate.

surface.name: role_at_least
surface.intent: Role-ordering check — instead of hardcoding a role order.

surface.name: accept_invitation
surface.intent: Resolve a pending invitation into a membership — entitlement check, first-login policies, emits together.

surface.name: apply_first_login_policies
surface.intent: Demand an org's first-login steps of an account, failing closed.

surface.name: create_invitation
surface.intent: Create a single-use, TTL'd invitation and best-effort deliver it.

surface.name: create_workspace
surface.intent: Create a workspace and atomically seed its owner membership — instead of a bare, ownerless row.

surface.name: decline_invitation
surface.intent: The invitee's terminal "no" (≠ revoke), same row-lock as accept.

surface.name: enforce_require_mfa
surface.intent: Sweep a workspace's members via auth.mfa_status, suspend the unenrolled, fail-open on an auth hiccup.

surface.name: ensure_personal_workspace
surface.intent: Idempotent get-or-create of a user's Personal workspace; prefer resolve_landing_workspace.

surface.name: issue_invitation_login_grant
surface.intent: Mint an auth-backed login grant for a not-yet-registered invitee's claim step (0.7).

surface.name: lift_deactivation_suspensions_for_user
surface.intent: Reverse deactivation suspensions on reactivation, leaving no_mfa ones alone.

surface.name: lift_no_mfa_suspensions
surface.intent: Lift every no_mfa suspension in a workspace — call when require_mfa turns off.

surface.name: lift_no_mfa_suspensions_for_user
surface.intent: Lift a user's no_mfa suspensions only, wired to auth's user.mfa_enabled.

surface.name: provision_member
surface.intent: Create an org-provisioned member end to end (debit, auth.provision_user, membership, credentials).

surface.name: resend_invitation
surface.intent: Rotate an invitation's token, extend its TTL and re-deliver — instead of editing fields by hand.

surface.name: reset_member_password
surface.intent: Reset a member's password on the org's order, with the audit emit and security-signal letter.

surface.name: resolve_landing_workspace
surface.intent: The canon landing-mandate policy (mandate-model vardict 2026-08-03) for a freshly (re)appearing account — call this from a user.registered subscriber instead of unconditionally minting a personal workspace; reads STREET_LANDING_MODE and is a deliberate no-op for an invited origin, so a subscriber cannot double-mint or race the invite's own membership.

surface.name: revoke_invitation
surface.intent: Withdraw a live invitation under the same compare-and-set lock as accept/decline.

surface.name: security_settings_for
surface.intent: Typed, defaulted view of Workspace.settings["security"] — instead of indexing the JSON bag directly.

surface.name: suspend_member
surface.intent: Suspend a membership without removing it (idempotent) — instead of writing suspended_at directly.

surface.name: suspend_memberships_for_deactivated_user
surface.intent: Suspend every membership of a deactivated account, wired to auth's user.deactivated.

surface.name: suspend_memberships_without_mfa
surface.intent: Per-user no_mfa suspension sweep wired to auth's user.mfa_disabled — call to force it on demand.

surface.name: unsuspend_member
surface.intent: Lift a membership suspension (idempotent) — counterpart of suspend_member.

requires.reason: comm bus (workspace.* emits, workspaces.check_membership Function, user.registered consumer), JWT authentication, GDPR provider registry

emits the user.registered event that triggers personal-workspace creation and issues the authenticated sessions the workspace endpoints require; answers auth.issue_login_grant for the invitation claim step and auth.provision_user / auth.mfa_status for org provisioning and the require_mfa sweep; answers auth.admin_reset_password (>= 0.18) for the administrative password reset — which is where the credential work, the session revocation, the audit row and the refusal to touch a staff account live, because the caller knows who administers a workspace and nothing about who administers the deployment; answers auth.apply_first_login_policies (>= 0.17) when an organization has CONFIGURED first-login policies — that seam alone is fail-closed: an acceptance that cannot raise a demanded policy is refused (503) rather than admitting an unhardened member, while an organization that configured nothing never calls it at all; every other auth seam either degrades to an honest 503 (claim) or is never reached; decoupled via the comm bus

delivers the letters this module requests via request_notification: workspace.invitation (create), workspace.invitation.reminder (admin resend, >= 0.6.1), workspace.member_password_reset (>= 0.6.1) and the workspace.provisioned_account / workspace.mfa_* family; every one is best-effort — the workspace operation succeeds regardless, and an older notifications catalog drops the unknown type with a logged error
answers billing.check_entitlement for org creation and member-seat ceilings; without it every entitlement check degrades to allow (OSS default), decoupled via the comm bus
